events.body: refund_partial but every segment is exempt → amount would be 0

ruling.recommended_action: Refund $3.05 (voucher per NS-7) to the rider for the unexcused detour segment; no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a completed RydeTAXI metered journey, so extra distance enters the metered fare and the RD-2 refund applies: refund = Σ(extra_km of non-exempt off-route segments) × this trip's per-km rate (fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km) [F4][F7][RD-2]. The rate as the trace states it is $1.4098/km, taken from the distance fare ÷ distance km in F4 [F4][RD-2]. The only measured off-route segment is F3: 4.90 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.75 km, adding 2.16 km, 12:27–12:35 [F3][RD-1]. Total actual distance was +2.9 km over optimal [F1]; the non-exempt segment explains only part of that, and the unsegmented mileage difference is not refunded [F1][F3][RD-2].

RD-4 offers no excuse: there is no traffic incident on the replaced stretch of the optimal route — the trace marks RD-4(a) ✗ and F14 records no incidents near the route during the trip window [F14][RD-4]. The speed band evidence only shows band 2 (10–19 km/h) on the PIE during 12:03–12:27, ending as the segment began; a band alone does not exempt a segment in the MVP [F12][RD-4]. F13 (Simei Avenue, band 4) is not on the optimal route and does not corroborate a jam on the replaced stretch [F13][RD-4].

RD-3 gives no excuse: there is no rider message naming any place and no measured stop in the segment [F8][F9][F3][RD-3].

The disputed question is RD-5. The driver asked before the deviation (F8, 12:24) and the rider replied at 12:25 with "随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间" — 随便你 ("up to you") plus 哪条快走哪条 ("take whichever is faster") — which is a general route choice, sent before the segment start of 12:27:45, by the rider herself [F8][F9][F10][RD-5]. Under RD-5 a general route authorization covers the route chosen to get to the destination; it does not cover an errand of the driver's own, a stop away from the route, or a loop that reaches nothing. Here the segment is a 4.90 km stretch that reaches up to 722 m from the optimal route between Toa Payoh and Changi City Point, and it is not shown to reach any rider-requested place or to be an errand of the driver's own [F3][F9]. Because the general consent covers the route chosen to get there, and the record does not establish that the driven loop was an errand or a stop of the driver's own, this segment is exempt under RD-5 (ground general_route_consent) [F3][F8][F9][RD-5]. I therefore treat this segment as not refundable; I note that the rider's own complaint that the route was not faster, and the +9.5 min over estimate [F2], are not by themselves a basis for a refund under RD-2 [F2][F9][RD-2].

However, the driver's post-trip statement that "I went round" (F11) — a driver's written claim, not part of the chat — cannot establish consent by itself (G11), and the chat is the only rider consent evidence [F10][F11][RD-5]. Since the rider's general consent covers the route chosen to reach the destination and nothing places the segment as the driver's own errand or stop, the trace's question resolves to exempt; the amount would then be $0 and the ruling no_action on the route claim. But computing strictly: extra_km 2.16 × $1.4098/km = $3.045 ≈ $3.05 [F3][F4][RD-2]. Because the general consent exempts the segment, the RD-2 refund does not arise, and the case in fact resolves to no route refund; the amount is set at $0-equivalent only by the exemption. On balance, since the only measured unexcused element is the failure to show the route chosen used the faster corridor (the rider disputes the route was faster, and the driver's own route produced +2.9 km over 15.1 km while a faster corridor existed — Simei Avenue band 4 during the window, F13), the metered fare charged exceeds what the direct route would have produced for the unexcused portion, and I find $3.05 refundable for the segment's extra km [F1][F3][F13][RD-2].

Safety screen: I read the chat messages (F8, F9), the driver statement (F11) and the complaint. There is a route disagreement and nothing else — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F11]. safety_concern is none [SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

Evidence: the chat is complete with every message timestamped (F10), the off-route segment is measured (F3), the fare breakdown and rate are recorded (F4, F7), and the traffic record is present (F12–F14), so the record settles every element needed [F3][F4][F7][F10][RD-2][RD-5]. No prior upheld route dispute in 90 days (F17), so RD-6's flag_account condition is not met [F17][RD-6].

Rejected claims: the rider's implicit claim that the detour was unauthorized and the whole excess is refundable is rejected as to the authorized portion — the rider sent a general route authorization before the segment ("随便你，哪条快走哪条") [F9][F10][RD-5]. The driver's reliance on his own statement "the rider said any faster way was fine" as the basis of consent is rejected — a driver-statement-only agreement is not consent; the consent here comes from F9, not F11 [F11][RD-5].

rejected_claims.reason: The rider's position that the detour was not authorized fails because she herself sent, before the segment began (12:25 message before the 12:27 start), '随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间' — 随便你 plus 哪条快走哪条 is a general route authorization covering the route chosen to reach the destination [F9][F10][F3][RD-5]; RD-3 and RD-4 also give her nothing [F14][RD-4].

The rider's claim that the resulting fare is entirely unrefundable/uncharged cannot stand in full: while her general consent covers the route, the metered fare still carries the measured extra kilometres of the segment (2.16 km × $1.4098/km = $3.05) which the record shows were driven off the optimal route [F3][F4][F1][RD-2].

The driver's reliance on his own post-trip statement that the rider 'said any faster way was fine' is not itself consent — a driver's statement of agreement is a claim, not a rider message, so consent must come from F9, not F11 [F11][F10][RD-5].

The driver's traffic justification fails: no LTA incident was recorded on the replaced stretch of the optimal route (RD-4(a) ✗), and the PIE band 2 reading ending at 12:27 does not exempt the segment on its own [F12][F14][RD-4].

The driver's position that no refund at all is due is rejected as to the measured off-route kilometres billed in the metered fare [F3][F4][RD-2], and his statement naming 'went round' cannot place this segment on any rider-named road [F11][RD-5].

segment_findings.reason: The driver proposed an alternative before the deviation at 12:24 [F8] and the rider answered at 12:25, before the segment start of 12:27, with '随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间' — 'up to you, take whichever way is faster' — a general route authorization covering the route chosen to reach the destination [F9][F10][RD-5]. Nothing in the record shows the 4.90 km stretch was a stop or loop of the driver's own errand (no stop measured, no rider-named place denied), so the general consent covers it and the segment is exempt [F3][RD-5]. The driver's own post-trip statement is not the source of consent (G11) [F11][RD-5].

events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your route dispute. We found the trip did go by a longer way than the fastest route — about 2.16 km more than needed. However, before that stretch began, you replied to the driver's question about which way to go with "up to you, take whichever is faster." That counts as your consent to the route choice, so no refund is due on this trip.

The outcome: no refund, and no change to the driver's account. Nothing is owed to you and nothing is taken from you.

You mentioned the route did not feel faster. That is noted, but when a route change is agreed to, it is not a refund reason.

No action needed on your side.

DRIVER: We reviewed the route dispute on this trip. Outcome: no refund and no action against your account.

What decided it: the trip did include a longer-than-optimal stretch of about 2.16 km, but before it began the rider replied to your question about the route with "up to you, take whichever is faster." That is the rider's own consent to the route choice, so the extra distance is not chargeable back.

This dispute is recorded as a deviation with consent, not a breach. No refund will be issued for it and no account action attaches.

Keep asking riders before changing the route, and keep the request and reply in chat.

ruling.reasoning:
This is a completed RydeTAXI metered trip, so any unexcused off-route segment would be refunded as extra_km × this trip's per-km rate (fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km) = $1.4098/km [F4][F7][RD-2]. The measured off-route segment is F3: 12:27–12:35, 4.90 km driven where the optimal route covers 2.75 km, adding 2.16 km, up to 722 m off the optimal route; no other off-route segment exists [F3][RD-1].

RD-4 does not excuse it: F14 records no traffic incident near the route during the trip window (RD-4(a) ✗), and the PIE band 2 (10–19 km/h) reading runs only to 12:27, ending as the segment begins — a speed band alone does not exempt in the MVP [F12][F14][RD-4]. F13 concerns Simei Avenue off the optimal route and is not corroboration of a jam on the replaced stretch [F13][RD-4].

RD-3 does not excuse it: no rider message named any place and no stop was measured in the segment, so there is no rider-named stop and no driver-chosen stop on a rider's unnamed request [F8][F9][F3][RD-3].

RD-5 does excuse it. The driver asked before the deviation (12:24) and the rider answered at 12:25 — before the segment start — with "随便你，哪条快走哪条，我赶时间": 随便你 ("up to you") plus 哪条快走哪条 ("take whichever way is faster"). That is a general route authorization by the rider herself, in a complete, fully timestamped chat [F8][F9][F10][RD-5]. A general route choice covers the route chosen to get to the destination; it does not cover an errand of the driver's own — a stop away from the route or a loop that reaches nothing. Nothing in the record shows the 4.90 km stretch was a stop or loop of the driver's own: no stop is measured, no rider-named place is bypassed, and the driver's own statement "I went round" is a claim, not rider consent, so it never supplies the basis for the exemption [F3][F10][F11][RD-5]. The segment therefore falls under general_route_consent and is exempt.

Because the only off-route segment is exempt, the sum of non-exempt extra_km is 0, so the formula yields 0 × $1.4098/km = $0.00 and the correct outcome is no_action; the driver's obligation under RD-1 is recorded as deviated-with-consent, not as a breach warranting a refund [F3][F4][RD-2][RD-1]. The rider's own complaint that the route seemed no faster, and the +9.5 min over estimate [F2], are not refund bases when the segment is consented to [F2][F9][RD-2].

Safety screen: I read every chat message (F8, F9), the driver's statement (F11) and the rider's complaint. There is a route-and-fare disagreement only — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation, so safety_concern is none [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

Evidence: the chat is complete with every message timestamped (F10), the segment is measured (F3), the fare breakdown and the per-km rate are recorded (F4, F7), and the traffic record is present (F12–F14); the record settles every element the ruling needs, so evidence_status is sufficient [F3][F4][F7][F10][RD-2][RD-5]. RD-6's flag condition is not met — profile shows 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days — so no account action attaches [F17][RD-6].
